questions.q: Why is OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials grant the right fit for ServiceNow calling Meridian HR, rather than Authorization Code grant?
options: Authorization Code grant is faster to configure
Client Credentials is the only grant type ServiceNow supports at all
Authorization Code assumes a human user logging in to delegate access; this is a server-to-server call with no user involved
Client Credentials doesn't require a client ID or secret
questions.explain: Client Credentials grant exists exactly for backend-to-backend calls with no human user in the loop.

questions.q: Looking at `var r = new sn_ws.RESTMessageV2('MeridianHR', 'getEmployee');`, what do the two constructor arguments identify?
options: A username and password
The REST Message name and the specific Function to call within it
The OAuth Token URL and the scope
The sys_user table and a field name
questions.explain: The two strings name the REST Message record and the specific Function configured inside it, exactly as Lesson 6 established.

questions.q: Once the OAuth Entity Profile is attached to the MeridianHR REST Message, what happens to the bearer token?
options: RESTMessageV2 requests and refreshes it automatically — no manual Authorization header is ever written in script
The developer must manually add it to every request header in script
It's hardcoded once and never refreshed
It's unnecessary because Meridian HR doesn't check it
questions.explain: Attaching the OAuth profile to the REST Message is what lets RESTMessageV2 handle the entire token lifecycle on its own.

questions.q: In the webhook handler code, what does `response.setStatus(202)` signal, and why is pulling the employee record inline acceptable here?
options: It signals a fatal error; inline pulling is never acceptable
It acknowledges the webhook was accepted; inline pulling is acceptable because this integration's new-hire volume is low
It means authentication failed
It triggers Meridian HR to resend the same webhook immediately
questions.explain: 202 acknowledges acceptance of the request; processing inline is a reasonable simplification only because volume here is genuinely low.

questions.q: Why doesn't the pullEmployeeFromMeridian script ever reference an OAuth token directly?
options: Because Meridian HR doesn't actually require authentication
Because the token is passed in as a hardcoded string
Because OAuth isn't compatible with RESTMessageV2
Because the OAuth Entity Profile attached to the REST Message record handles requesting, attaching, and refreshing the token entirely outside the script
questions.explain: That separation — token handling living in configuration, not script — is exactly what makes OAuth the production-grade choice.
